adaptation: Standard layout adapted: the chart anchors on total money in (revenue $76.2M + other income $797.8M = $874.0M) because a $728.4M non-cash warrant fair-value gain dwarfs revenue. Balance checks on the adapted model: total money in = left after direct costs + cost of revenue ($874.0M = $848.8M + $25.2M); left after direct costs = profit after running costs + operating expenses ($848.8M = $709.6M + $139.3M). Reported figures are unchanged: revenue $76.2M, gross profit $51.0M, operating loss $88.2M, other income $797.8M, tax $0.0M, net income $709.5M.

opex.name: Power & site operations
opex.note: Running the data centers day to day — electricity, staff and maintenance, including $1.7M paid to related parties.

opex.name: Selling, general & administrative
opex.note: The back office: executives, finance and legal. Up from $17M a year ago as the company scaled up and paid more stock-based compensation.

opex.name: Depreciation
opex.note: Spreading the cost of buildings and equipment over their working lives — a non-cash charge.

opex.name: Impairment & disposal losses
opex.note: Writing down equipment ($9.7M) and losses on disposals ($3.9M), partly offset by a $0.6M gain on digital assets held.

follow100Note: Per $100 of total money in ($874M), not per $100 of revenue: $91 of every $100 that 'came in' was gains — $83 of it the non-cash warrant revaluation alone. Measured against revenue alone, the gains would be about $1,050 per $100.
footerNote: Net income is the consolidated figure; $709.9M was attributable to TeraWulf Inc. after noncontrolling interests absorbed a $0.4M loss. Figures are rounded to $M; the $0.03M tax provision rounds to $0.

kpis.label: Revenue growth
kpis.note: Revenue was $76M, vs $51M a year ago

kpis.label: EPS (GAAP basic)
kpis.note: Diluted EPS was -$0.03 — if warrant holders converted, the warrant gain would reverse

kpis.label: HPC lease revenue
kpis.note: 83% of all revenue, up from $7M a year ago

kpis.label: Operating loss
kpis.note: The running business lost money; Adjusted EBITDA was -$12.8M

oneTimers: A $728M non-cash gain from the change in fair value of warrant and derivative liabilities — the biggest single line of the quarter. It reverses if the warrants gain value again.
A $95M gain on the sale of an equity interest in an investee — a stake TeraWulf sold during the quarter.
Impairment of property, plant and equipment of $9.7M, plus $3.9M of losses on equipment disposals.
otherDetail: Other income was $798M, net: a $728M non-cash gain from the change in fair value of warrant and derivative liabilities, a $95M gain on selling an equity stake, and $29M of interest income, less $54M of interest expense and a $0.5M share of a joint venture's loss.

segments.name: HPC lease revenue
segments.note: Renting powered data-center space to AI and high-performance-computing customers — the Lake Mariner campus in New York. Up from $7M a year ago as new capacity started earning rent.

segments.name: Digital asset revenue
segments.note: Bitcoin TeraWulf mines itself. Down 69% as power and space are shifted away from mining toward HPC leasing.

takeaways.text: Revenue rose 51% to $76.2M, and $63.0M of it — 83% — came from HPC leases (long-term rentals of powered data-center space to AI customers), up from just $7.2M a year ago. Bitcoin mining revenue fell 69% to $13.2M as power is redirected to leasing. After quarter-end, TeraWulf signed a 20-year lease with Anthropic worth roughly $19B of contracted revenue.
takeaways.title: AI rent is now the business

takeaways.text: Net income was $709.5M, but $728M of it is a non-cash gain: TeraWulf's warrant liabilities fell in value, and accounting rules book that as income. Operations themselves lost $88.2M, and the company's own Adjusted EBITDA was -$12.8M. Diluted EPS was actually -$0.03, because converting the warrants would erase the gain.
takeaways.title: The profit is paper, not cash

takeaways.text: Interest expense jumped to $53.6M in the quarter, from $9.8M a year ago, as TeraWulf borrows heavily to build data centers. It ended the quarter with 102 MW of capacity earning rent and another 336 MW under construction.
takeaways.title: Debt is getting expensive

verdict: TeraWulf's revenue jumped 51% to $76M as renting data-center space to AI customers became 83% of the business — but the $710M headline profit is a paper gain on its own warrants, not cash from a business that still lost $88M running itself.
